set.tovw: Lead grade B (treasure thread): two separate wire accounts plus the placed family farm
set.st: Nov 1935: Fred Noyes of Ludington said gold he had buried about 30 years earlier was still on his former farm in Eden Township near Scottville, by then owned by another family; AP put it at $85,000, other copies at $25,000. He had lost the map, and the rail fence and house used as landmarks were gone. He got a federal search warrant (gold-coin ban) and dug with a federal agent; a day's digging failed. The 1904 Mason County atlas lists a Noyes farm in sec. 5, Eden Township (settled 1880). Pin is the 1904 house mark on the family 80, not the spot itself. Censuses show Fred farmed in Eden Township with his father from at least 1910 to 1920 and lived in Ludington by 1930.
pinev: 1904 Standard Atlas of Mason County: Noyes 80 (SW¼ NW¼ sec. 5 + SE¼ NE¼ sec. 6 T17N R16W) with the house mark on the 5/6 line, placed from the BLM PLSS grid; 300 m covers the whole 80
S. J. = Samuel J. Noyes, Fred's father (1910 census: Fred S. Noyes with his father Samuel J. in Eden Twp; 1920 Eden; 1930 Ludington).
Two separate wire services (INS, AP) plus the Detroit News' own report; placed family farm = B.

src: US census 1910, 1920 Eden Twp and 1930 Ludington, Mason Co MI (Ancestry, PC (b)); research/ancestry/noyes-mason-census.md
